rationale: Tests recall of Bloor's lipid classification terms and fatty acid omega/delta nomenclature, the foundational vocabulary established across blocks 3–4.
Tests understanding of the ordered sequence of dietary fat digestion and absorption from duodenum to bloodstream, the central process established in block 6.
Tests recall of the carnitine shuttle mechanism and beta-oxidation energy yield, the key mechanistic details of fatty acid oxidation in block 8.

Tests understanding of cholesterol synthesis regulation — the rate-limiting enzyme, its product, compartment distinction from ketogenesis, and pharmacological inhibition — the key concepts in block 13.

Tests the ability to identify the four key steps of eicosanoid metabolism — arachidonic acid release, the COX and LOX branches, and drug inhibition — on a visual schematic, applying the pathway from block 14.
Provides an interactive visual explorer of the four major lipoprotein classes — size, density, core composition and key apolipoproteins — consolidating the structural overview in block 17.
Tests understanding of the input–output imbalance underlying fatty liver, cholelithiasis and obesity — the unifying biochemical framework established in block 21.
Tests the ability to identify which specific findings in a lipid profile report invalidate the Friedewald LDL estimate, applying the interpretation rules from block 23 to a clinical scenario.
